scope: Four authentic archival map records, including a Canada-related map. Primary LOC guide and full archive-record text returned by web search were read. Direct item requests returned 403; no image was successfully viewed. All four remain link-only pending actual image inspection. No images downloaded, Site edits, contact or delegation.

items.historicalTitle: [Map of the several nations of Indians to the Northwest of South Carolina]
items.creator: Unidentified Indigenous maker; colonial copy associated with Francis Nicholson
items.dateNote: Guide dates presentation of the underlying Indigenous draught approximately 1721.
items.rightsStatement: Reuse permitted unless an item-specific Rights Advisory states otherwise.
items.creditLine: Library of Congress, Geography and Map Division.
items.annotation: An archival reproduction preserves a copied network of communities and paths drawn from Indigenous knowledge. The conventional Catawba title does not establish the maker’s identity. Colonial annotations and multiple copying stages make its production history essential context for interpretation.

items.historicalTitle: Copy of a sketch of the Monongahela, with the field of battle,
items.creator: John Montrésor associated; unidentified Indigenous direction credited
items.rightsStatement: Reuse permitted unless an item-specific Rights Advisory states otherwise.
items.creditLine: Library of Congress, Geography and Map Division.
items.annotation: This battlefield sketch credits Indigenous direction, while the catalog associates it with John Montrésor. That wording exposes a history of mediation and copying. It offers a focused example of Indigenous geographic knowledge entering a colonial military record, with its maker unnamed.

items.historicalTitle: A map of the inhabited part of Canada from the French surveys, with the frontiers of New York and New England;
items.creator: Claude Joseph Sauthier; William Faden
items.dateNote: Guide thumbnail corresponds to digital copy ar015201.
items.rightsStatement: Reuse permitted unless an item-specific Rights Advisory states otherwise.
items.creditLine: Library of Congress, Geography and Map Division.
items.annotation: A British colonial map of southern Quebec and neighboring borderlands, compiled from French surveys. Its military and commercial framing offers evidence about colonial priorities and representations of Indigenous people. Read it as a historical viewpoint, without treating it as present territorial authority.

items.historicalTitle: Manatvs gelegen op de Noot [sic] Riuier
items.creator: Joan Vinckeboons
items.dateNote: Record: created 1639, indexed 1670. Guide: copied around 1665 after a 1639 map.
items.rightsStatement: Public domain or no known copyright restrictions; reuse permitted.
items.creditLine: Library of Congress, The Atlantic World: America and the Netherlands.
items.annotation: This Dutch colonial map records settlements and landholding around Manhattan; Indigenous villages also appear in the archive’s guide. It invites comparison of ways of naming and representing inhabited places. The catalog and guide give differing dates for the surviving copy.

inspectionNotes.imageUrlProvenance: All four exact IIIF image URLs were observed in img src attributes in the primary LOC guide's actual HTML, paired with their corresponding item links. They are observed preview URLs, not invented or guessed full-resolution endpoints.
inspectionNotes.recordTextMethod: Domain-restricted searches returned full primary LOC item-record bodies, including catalog names, dates, notes, Digital IDs and Rights & Access text. This is more than a title snippet, but remains cached record-text inspection. Direct HTML item and ordinary public JSON requests returned 403. No authentication, browser challenge or certificate warning bypassed.
inspectionNotes.imageVerificationLimits: The Catawba image URL timed out in the web tool. No browser surface was available to this child; image searches returned no viewable results. No successful image-pixel inspection is claimed for any item. Parent may retain these as link-only entries or perform a separate authorized image/rights match before a preview.
inspectionNotes.rightsVerificationLimits: Rights statements and short exact quotes above were read in the cached primary records. The first three use LOC's conditional Geography and Map collection statement, and no item-specific restriction appeared in the returned text. Manhattan uses the Atlantic World public-domain/no-known-restrictions statement. These facts are not a new blanket license for unrelated copies, every repository version, or altered/source-derived illustrations. No actual preview is authorized by this packet's publicationMode field.
dateAndAuthorshipLimits: Catawba: distinguish the 1929 archival reproduction, the early eighteenth-century copied map, and the earlier Indigenous draught. The primary guide says the maker was likely Catawba or Cherokee; an exact nation and individual are not established. Nicholson is an associated colonial recipient/dedicator, not identified as the original Indigenous maker.

Monongahela: the catalog notes insertion of 'direction of' between 'By' and 'an Indian.' Credit Indigenous guidance without silently converting the mediated sketch into an unqualified named Indigenous-authored original.
Canada and Manhattan: these are European colonial cartography, not established Indigenous-authored maps. Indigenous representation or place names do not establish authorship.
Manhattan's record created/published year, index/citation date and guide's copying date differ. Display the distinction, rather than select a falsely certain surviving-object date.
inspectionNotes.fullResolutionLimits: The readable records expose archival viewer Digital IDs and download controls, but no direct full-resolution download URL was recovered. Null values are intentional. No URLs generated by modifying IIIF size/format parameters.
inspectionNotes.presentationLimits: Historical titles retain old spellings and terminology as source metadata. Every entry must be labeled historical and attributed. These documents are evidence of historical perspectives, copying and power; they are not authoritative current tribal boundaries or exhaustive descriptions of peoples.
inspectionNotes.scopeStop: Exactly four selected map records. Gallatin/Powell are assigned separately. No more discovery, image downloading, Site edits, generated images, contact or delegation.

wordBudgetCheck.method: Conservative whitespace counts include all item string values except URLs and record IDs, including titles/credits/rights and inspection labels.
